text: Chapter one gave you the mechanics of a flow — triggers, actions, conditions, HTTP calls. AI Builder is where that changes: it's Power Platform's layer of AI models that you drop into a flow as an action, so a step can read a document or generate text instead of just moving data around.

AI Builder isn't a separate product — it lives inside the same environment as your flows, reachable through AI hub in Power Automate's navigation. And several of its capabilities, especially prompts, actually run on Azure AI services underneath, including Azure OpenAI. You'll go deeper on that connection in lesson twelve. For now, just know that an AI Builder action and an HTTP action are closer cousins than they look.

Every model is either prebuilt or custom. Prebuilt models are ready the moment you open AI Builder — Microsoft already trained them on general data. Custom models you train yourself, on your own samples. At Castlebridge Logistics, our example company this chapter, a document processing model trained on their specific delivery confirmation layout is a custom model — nobody else's data taught it what a Castlebridge PDF looks like.
This is AI hub's Explore screen — the catalog where every model category you'll use this chapter starts: prebuilt and custom alike, all in one place.

This chapter only needs three categories out of that whole catalog. Document processing extracts fields and tables from PDFs. Classification sorts text or images into categories. And prompts generate text, summaries, or structured JSON from a generative model. Each one gets its own lesson, in that order, building toward one combined flow by the end of the chapter.
Up next, lesson eight: teaching a document processing model to read an actual Castlebridge Logistics delivery confirmation.
